muted.source: dist/style.css :root --muted (second, effective declaration; the first is #627166)

display.purpose: One two-tone page headline per surface; ink first line, second voice on the second line.

headline.purpose: Section openers and the inverted closing invitation.

title.purpose: Ledger terms, step names, desk headings.

body.purpose: Prose capped at 48-65ch; muted for support, ink for the load-bearing sentence.

amount.purpose: Every figure the reader is asked to accept: statement lines, service prices, plan figures. Always tabular.

label.purpose: Field labels, desk table column headers, stacked-row data labels. Never above a heading.

shadows.name: modal-lift
shadows.purpose: The study dialog only, over a blurred #06130dbc backdrop. The only shadow in the system; surfaces otherwise separate by ground change or rule.

motion.name: amount-settle
motion.purpose: The one authored motion: offer statement amounts settle on first paint and on redate. Off under reduced motion.

motion.name: state-feedback
motion.purpose: Button and text-link hover/active; active nudges translateY(1px).

motion.name: control-feedback
motion.purpose: Choice rows and field state changes.

motion.name: sheet-slide
motion.purpose: The phone sticky action bar and rail movement.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { *, *::before, *::after { animation: none !important; transition: none !important } html { scroll-behavior: auto } }
motion.purpose: Global off switch; every surface inherits it.

narrative.overview:
Veylet's surfaces read like a well-kept ledger left on good paper: a warm off-white ground, near-black green ink, hairline rules that divide without enclosing, and numbers set so a changed figure shifts nothing on the line. Nothing is boxed to look important; importance is carried by position, rule weight and the size of the number. The system has one accent and spends it rarely.

Density is editorial rather than dashboard. Marketing surfaces run wide (1456px container, 20-64px fluid gutter) with generous chapter breaks, while the signed-in desk and studio use the same materials at a tighter rhythm: the same hairlines, the same tabular figures, a real table instead of a card grid. A visitor moving from /offer to the desk should feel they walked into the back office of the same firm, not a different product.

The system's one authored motion is the offer statement's amounts settling from muted to ink over 240ms; everything else is state feedback measured in fifths of a second. Reduced motion switches all of it off globally.
keyCharacteristics: Ink #10231d on paper #f4f1e9; one sage accent and no second accent colour.
Hairline rules and ground changes carry structure; the build ships no card shadows.
Square corners on marketing surfaces; a 2px radius only where a control must read as a control.
Money and counts are always tabular numerals, right-aligned, in a statement.
44px minimum target on every stand-alone action; visible focus everywhere.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Sage marks the moment something changes: money first changes hands, a sort becomes active, a plan is good. If a surface uses sage more than once or twice, it is decorating, not marking.

rules.name: The Ink-and-Paper Rule
rules.body: There are two grounds, paper and ink, and nothing in between. Tint (#eaece3) is a note, not a third ground.

rules.name: The Two-Tone Headline Rule
rules.body: A page headline is two lines and two voices: the statement in ink, the promise in the second voice (deep sage Outfit on the homepage, Georgia italic on /offer). Never three tones, never a third line.

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Every amount, count and allowance is font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums, 500 weight, right-aligned in its ledger, with its qualifier set beneath in muted fine type. A changed number must not move the layout.

rules.name: The 44px Rule
rules.body: Every stand-alone action, summary, field and desk control carries min-height: 44px (52px for refined marketing buttons). Inline text links inside a paragraph are exempt; nothing else is.

rules.name: The Ground-Change Rule
rules.body: To separate a thing from the page, flip its ground or rule it off. Do not lift it.

dos: Do build structure from hairlines and definition lists (1px #ccd2c5, 2px ink to open or total). A new section is rules and spacing, not a container.
Do set every amount, count and allowance in tabular numerals at 500 weight, right-aligned, with its qualifier beneath in muted fine type.
Do keep page headlines two-tone and two-line, and keep the second voice to the one the surface already uses.
Do give every stand-alone action a 44px target, a visible focus ring, and a label that says what happens.
Do use the fixed plan-state strings verbatim on every surface that shows plan state.
Do honour prefers-reduced-motion: the global reset kills animation and transitions, and the statement's settle must stay off.
Do keep marketing corners square; reserve 2px for controls and rounding above 8px for device-like or status chrome.
donts: Don't put an eyebrow, kicker or tracked-caps line above a heading. /offer ships without one, and the plain-case .for-line is what replaced it; 11px uppercase is for field labels and table columns only.
Don't make cards the structure. No three-up pricing cards, no bordered feature tiles; the ledger is the structure.
Don't add shadows to lift a surface. Change the ground or add a rule.
Don't introduce a second accent colour, a second sans face, or a weight outside 400/500.
Don't invent proof: no testimonials, counters, logos, statistics or customer examples exist, and the studies are labelled studies.
Don't add motion theatre. One authored motion (the 240ms amount settle) plus 0.2s state feedback is the whole budget.
Don't load a third-party script, font or icon set at runtime. Outfit is self-hosted, the mark and markers are CSS.
Don't add a custom widget where a native control exists (date, select, details).
